title: About GeoUnpack
description: Who makes GeoUnpack, why it exists, how it converts Esri files locally in your browser, what it can't do yet, and how to get in touch.
html:
GeoUnpack is a small independent tool made by Jiayi (GitHub), an independent developer based in Canada. It exists because people regularly receive ArcGIS layer packages, map packages and file geodatabases without having an ArcGIS licence, and the free workarounds (renaming files, installing QGIS, using command-line GDAL) are not obvious to everyone.

How it works

When you drop a file, your browser unpacks it with 7-Zip and reads it with the open-source GDAL library, both compiled to WebAssembly. The conversion runs on your own computer. Your files are never uploaded, and there is no account or server-side storage.

What it can and can't do

  • Opens .lpk, .lpkx, .mpk, .mpkx and zipped .gdb files, KML and KMZ files, and shapefiles (the .shp, .shx, .dbf and .prj files together, or a .zip of them).
  • Exports vector layers and tables to Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KML, KMZ and CSV.
  • Not supported yet: raster, tile and scene packages, symbology and labels, files over 150 MB.

Always keep your original file and check converted data before relying on it.

Open source

The code that finds the data inside .lpk and .mpk packages is published as an open-source library: gis-package-unpack (MIT).

Other tools by the same developer: Find Shutter Count — check a camera's shutter count from a photo, in your browser.

Independence

GeoUnpack is not affiliated with or endorsed by Esri. It uses only open-source libraries, listed on the licenses page.

Contact

Found a file that doesn't convert, or have a suggestion? Email hello@geounpack.com. Sample files that fail (if you are allowed to share them) help the most.

title: Privacy
description: GeoUnpack does not upload or store your files.
html:
Your files never leave your computer. When you open a file, it is read by code running in your browser. Nothing about the file's content is sent to us or to anyone else.

The conversion engine (the open-source GDAL library, about 11 MB) is downloaded from our own storage at cdn.geounpack.com the first time you open a file, and then cached by your browser. If that download fails, the same files are fetched from the public jsDelivr CDN instead; like any web request, that shows jsDelivr your IP address and browser type, but nothing about your file.

The map preview loads background map tiles from OpenStreetMap's tile servers; those requests contain only the map area being displayed (and, as with any web request, your IP address), not your data.

We use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts page views without cookies and without tracking you across sites.

To find out whether the converter works for people, the page also sends an anonymous count when something happens, for example "a file was opened", "a layer was exported to GeoPackage" or "an export failed because the browser ran out of memory". Only daily totals are stored: the event, the page it happened on, and a short category such as the file type, a size range or the output format. When a file fails to open, the count also notes which kind of archive the file is (for example 7-Zip or zip), read from its first few bytes. No file names, layer names, file contents, IP addresses or cookies are recorded, and the counts cannot be linked to you.

If you buy a licence in the future, payment is handled by our payment provider; we receive your email address and the purchase details only.

title: Open-source licenses
html:
GeoUnpack is built on these open-source projects. Thank you to their authors.

  • gdal3.js (GDAL compiled to WebAssembly): LGPL-2.1-or-later. GDAL itself is MIT/X licensed; bundled dependencies carry their own licenses. The unmodified library files (npm package gdal3.js@2.8.1) are served from cdn.geounpack.com, with the jsDelivr CDN as a backup; source code is available at the link above.
  • 7z-wasm (7-Zip compiled to WebAssembly): 7-Zip is licensed under the GNU LGPL with the unRAR restriction. Source: 7-zip.org.
  • Leaflet: BSD-2-Clause.
  • fflate: MIT.
  • @tmcw/togeojson (reads KML and KMZ): BSD-2-Clause, © Tom MacWright, Mapbox.
  • Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
